items.text: The United States Central Command says that they have redirected 55 vessels linked to Iran since reinstating the blockade last July. ((Middle East Eye))

Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appoints new leaders for Iran's military to replace their predecessors after they were killed during the initial Israel and U.S. airstrikes, including Ali Abdollahi as chief of staff, Kioumars Heydari as deputy commander, and Hossein Taeb as Basij commander. ((The Jerusalem Post)) ((Al-Monitor))
Аt least 13 people were killed, including a child, and 39 others were injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on an oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, Russia. ((Reuters))
A earthquake strikes Chocó Department, Colombia, causing widespread and heavy damage, and killing at least 164 people. ((El Pais)) ((BBC News)) ((Reuters))

The Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary in Manizales is confirmed to be among the buildings damaged after one of the towers collapsed following the earthquake. ((The Independent)) ((The City Paper Bogota)) ((El Colombiano))
A recent wildfire at the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, is extinguished after were burnt. However, new hotspots are also reported near the caldera. ((Reuters))

The Philippine civil defense office reports that at least 16 people were killed across Luzon, including seven in Baguio, by floods, landslides and weather-related accidents after nine days of heavy monsoon rain, while three others remain missing. ((AFP via RFI)) ((ABS-CBN News))

The World Health Organization reports that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo started in February before its declaration, with some cases attributed to malaria and typhoid. ((Al Jazeera))

Colombia becomes the second country to recognize the Golan Heights, a region in southwestern Syria that has been under Israeli occupation since 1967, as part of Israel's sovereignty. ((The Jerusalem Post))

Upon petition from Rodina, the liberal Yabloko party is barred from participating in the 2026 Russian legislative election on charges of unregistered funding, a controversial copyright infringement, and extremism by the Supreme Court of Russia. ((The Guardian)) ((The Moscow Times))

In Pakistan, the Sindh government announces that a judicial commission headed by a judge of the Sindh High Court would investigate businessman Mir Raza Ali's death. The decision followed a recommendation by the Sindh Assembly. ((Dawn))

Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organization president Thongchai Yenprasert is killed in a shooting at a government building in Nonthaburi province, Thailand. Former parliament member Chalong Riewrang is taken into custody over corruption. ((BBC News)) ((AFP via CNA)) ((Thairath))
Аt least 13 people are killed, including a child, and 39 others were injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on an oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, Russia. ((Reuters))
Fawzi al-Mansouri, head of military intelligence for the Libyan National Army, is assassinated as a bomb exploded inside his car in Benghazi, Libya. ((AFP via RFI)) ((Al Jazeera))
A earthquake strikes Chocó Department, Colombia, causing widespread and heavy damage, and leaving at least 164 people dead. ((El Pais)) ((BBC News)) ((Reuters))

The Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary in Manizales is confirmed to be among the buildings damaged after one of the towers collapsed following the earthquake. ((The Independent)) ((The City Paper Bogota)) ((El Colombiano in Spanish))

The Philippine civil defense office reports that at least 16 people were killed across Luzon, including seven in Baguio, by floods, landslides and weather-related accidents after nine days of heavy monsoon rain, while three others remain missing. ((AFP via RFI))

Colombia becomes the second country to recognize the Golan Heights, a region in southwestern Syria that has been under Israeli occupation since 1967, as part of Israel's sovereignty. ((AFP via CNA)) ((The Jerusalem Post))

The government of Sindh, Pakistan, announces that a judicial commission headed by a judge of the Sindh High Court would investigate businessman Mir Raza Ali's death. The decision followed a recommendation by the Sindh Assembly. ((Dawn))
The United States Central Command says that they have redirected 55 vessels linked to Iran since reinstating the blockade in July. ((Middle East Eye))
